text:
maria: FYI — I put together a quick sketch for separating the rate-control plane from the admission plane. thinking about long-term maintainability and abuse isolation.
jonathan: Nice. Is this the "control plane for decisions, data plane for enforcement" split?
kevin: yeah that's the idea. keep admission fast (edge) and offload policy evaluation & scoring to a separate control service.
alisha: Curious about the TL;DR for failure modes. if control plane is slow, do we block all admissions?
maria: Good call. proposal: edge has a cached fallback policy with conservative defaults. control plane computes fine-grained scoring + abuse signals async and pushes diffs.
vanessa: Can you share the consistency model? sounds like we need eventual+versioned policies to avoid flapping.
maria: Exactly — every policy change gets a monotonically increasing policy_version. Edge uses last-known version, will accept requests if version <= current. Control pushes two artifacts: full snapshot and incremental deltas.
jonathan: How do we handle tenant-specific overrides? per-tenant policy blobs or encoded as weighted rules?
kevin: Keep them as separate per-tenant meta blobs. Control plane stores shared rules + tenant overlay. Edge merges overlay at lookup time. overlay = small, often cached.
alisha: What about telemetry? If control plane is evaluating heavy scoring (abuse heuristics), we need strong sampling & backpressure to avoid thundering.
maria: Plan: sampling + adaptive sampling. also bulk-upload endpoints for batched signals. Control plane exposes an ingest throttle and will downsample low-impact signals.
vanessa: Ops question — expected latency for policy lookup if control is healthy? need <1ms extra at edge ideally.
kevin: Edge should not call control synchronously on request path. local cache hit is 0.2-0.5ms. miss path is async refresh and a fallback rule applied immediately.
sre-bot: deploy: new control-plane prototype rolled to canary (cluster b). No incidents so far. :rocket:
maria: Implementation notes: 1) ackless delta push over gRPC stream with backpressure tokens; 2) snapshot store in S3-compatible blob; 3) policy versioning scheme = epoch.counter (e.g., 2026-03-01.42).
alisha: Security: tenant blobs encrypted with KMS and signed. control plane verifies signatures before pushing to edge.
jonathan: Edge cache invalidation — we should avoid cache storms on big rollouts. idea: staggered drain using per-zone jittered TTLs and grace periods.
vanessa: For rollouts we also need a canary knob to target certain customers to new policy rules. Can the control plane tag versions with rollout IDs?
maria: Yes, rollout_id in metadata. edges can opt-in via config flags to only apply certain rollout IDs.
kevin: Related: metrics contract — control emits policy_applied_{ok, fallback, stale} labels and tenant_id. Edge emits cache_hit/miss and applied_version. Must be coordinated.
alisha: One last tradeoff: do we keep scoring model in control (slow but accurate) or provide a tiny on-edge model for critical heuristics?
jonathan: Hybrid: critical cheap heuristics on-edge, heavy ML scoring in control. control can also send suggested adjustments to the on-edge heuristics.
maria: Next steps: i'll open an RFC PR with diagrams + state machine, call out metrics and rollout playbook. planning a follow-up sync next Wed.
vanessa: +1 on RFC. can you include a small simulation of cache miss rates and control QPS in the PR?
maria: will do. thanks everyone.
kevin: Thanks — huge win if we can reduce tight coupling and make abuse rules safer to iterate. :thumbsup:
